selection: All newly discovered matching records in this collection; no fixed paper-count quota.

papers.title: Tumor-versus-non-tumor T cell clonotype enrichment enables antigen-agnostic prioritization of tumor-reactive TCR candidates, supported by single-cell and spatial phenotyping
papers.authors: Seitz, V.; Franzen, J.; Gennermann, K.; Hirsch, B.; Schaper, S.; Droege, A.; Dreger, M.; Genzel, N.; Plassmann, S.; Bents, D.; Gloekler, J.; Conrad, T.; Loddenkemper, C.; Schmelz, K.; Morkel, M.; Trinks, A.; Krieger, T. G.; Kainmueller, D.; Hummel, M.; Hennig, S.; Horst, D.; Lennerz, V.; Elezkurtaj, S.
papers.abstract: Introduction: Identifying tumor-reactive T cell receptors (TCRs) remains challenging, particularly when tumor antigens are unknown. We investigated tumor-to-non-tumor (T/N) clonotype enrichment as an antigen-agnostic strategy for prioritizing candidate tumor-reactive TCRs, supported by single-cell and spatial phenotyping. Methods: We performed bulk and single-cell TCR repertoire sequencing of paired tumor and adjacent non-tumor tissues across 15 cases comprising lung, pancreatic, breast, and colorectal cancers. Selected clonotypes were further characterized by single-cell gene expression profiling and Xenium spatial transcriptomics in two pancreatic cancer cases. Results: Tumor-enriched clonotypes included Cluster-A, a public HLA-A*02:01-restricted TCR cluster preferentially enriched in tumors across 14 HLA-A*02:01-positive patients, with previously demonstrated tumor recognition. In one pancreatic cancer case, spatial analysis revealed that Cluster-A CD8 T cells were exclusively detected in tumor tissue, preferentially localized near malignant epithelial cells, and exhibited an antigen-experienced effector-memory phenotype with elevated granzyme A and K expression. In another pancreatic cancer case lacking Cluster-A, the six most frequent CD8 T cell clonotypes showed a graded association between T/N enrichment and tumor-associated features, with higher T/N ratios correlating with closer proximity to malignant cells and increased granzyme A and K expression. Conclusion: These findings support the T/N ratio as a robust primary criterion for prioritizing candidate tumor-reactive TCRs. Integration of single-cell and spatial transcriptomics provides complementary biological evidence of tumor association and a framework for selecting therapeutic TCR candidates when functional validation is limited.

papers.title: Development and validation of a machine learning-based cell death-immune prognostic model for risk stratification in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
papers.authors: Bai ZY, Yao C, Zhai YQ, Hou XY, Li YG, Weng ZP, Xu JQ, Xie XM, Yi TZ, Jin ZY, Wu XL.
papers.abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) shows marked prognostic heterogeneity, partly driven by interactions between regulated cell death and the tumor immune microenvironment. A framework integrating multiple cell-death programs with immune states is still lacking. This study integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data to characterize immune-cell-death interactions in DLBCL. Immune-cell-death-related genes were identified by intersecting differentially expressed genes with immune and cell-death gene sets. A cell-death-immune score (CDIS) was constructed using 101 machine-learning combinations and evaluated in three external cohorts. This study assessed immune infiltration, cell-death transcriptional programs, cell-cell communication, ligand-target interactions, pseudotime trajectories, drug connectivity, molecular docking and virtual perturbation. In vitro assays further tested BAFF stimulation and tamoxifen treatment in DLBCL cell lines. We identified 159 immune-cell-death-related genes and selected 16 genes from 25 candidates to construct the CDIS prognostic model; CoxBoost plus random survival forest ranked highest (mean C-index 0.703). High CDIS was associated with suppressed transcriptional programs of immunogenic cell death and an immune-cold microenvironment with M2-like macrophage enrichment. CDIS provides incremental value over International Prognostic Index (IPI), particularly within the IPI 2 stratum, where it significantly further distinguished high- from low-risk patients (5-year overall survival 63.6% vs. 42.7%; log-rank P = 0.012). Single-cell analysis localized model genes mainly to macrophages and identified an M2-like macrophage-BAFF/APRIL-malignant B-cell axis. Exogenous BAFF promoted DLBCL-cell proliferation and reduced apoptosis, whereas tamoxifen inhibited proliferation dose-dependently. CDIS serves as a complementary prognostic model to IPI, refining risk within IPI strata, and reveals a candidate mechanism centered on the M2-like macrophage-BAFF/APRIL-malignant B-cell axis.

papers.title: scINTILLA: Single-Cell Integrated Inference, Labelling, and Landscape Analysis for Assessing the Quality and Hidden Diversity of Cell Annotations
papers.authors: Kanannejad, S.; Bongiorni, N.; Nordera, E.; Redaelli, S.; Rusconi, I.; Zanin, R.; Giustacchini, A.; Chatterjee, S.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing has made it possible to build atlases of millions of cells, but the cell-type labels in these atlases are rarely checked once they are assigned. When a label covers a transcriptionally heterogeneous population, every analysis that depends on it inherits the problem, and automated label transfer in particular becomes unreliable. We present scINTILLA (Single-Cell Integrated Inference, Labelling, and Landscape Analysis), a framework that scores every label in an annotated dataset from three complementary signals: clustering confusion (neighbours that share a cluster but carry another label), label fragmentation (one label spread over several clusters) and supervised consistency (agreement, confidence and entropy of a classifier ensemble). The three signals are combined into a per-label quality score, scINTILLA-F, which can optionally be rank-fused with the Silhouette width. To test whether the score finds real annotation problems, we injected three kinds of known errors (merged labels, contaminated labels and over-split labels) into five Human Cell Atlas datasets, giving 150 perturbed annotations, and compared scINTILLA with the Silhouette baseline, kNN purity, SCCAF and ROGUE in a pre-registered analysis. The four best of the eleven methods that score every label were all scINTILLA-based. The fusion of scINTILLA-F with Silhouette ranked first (balanced AUROC 0.908; Silhouette 0.896, kNN purity 0.815, SCCAF 0.770) and improved on the Silhouette baseline in every atlas, and adding fragmentation raised the detection of merged labels in every atlas. scINTILLA and the Silhouette baseline were complementary. The Silhouette baseline was better at finding merges, whereas scINTILLA was better at finding over-split labels. Applied to the real atlases, scINTILLA flagged the ``Unknown'' and monocyte-derived macrophage labels of the lung atlas and the ``stem cell'' label of the endoderm organoid atlas. Re-analysis of these populations resolved disease-associated monocyte and macrophage states and a set of progenitor, stromal and differentiated identities with distinct tissue and protocol origins. Finally, we tested the score on merges that arise naturally, in a leukaemia atlas of 183 patients whose blast populations we had annotated. Label fragmentation revealed the diversity of the blasts hidden under a patient label: in acute myeloid leukaemia it was higher in patients whose blasts formed several populations. In each of these cases scINTILLA pointed to the labels that needed a closer look, and the interpretation remained with the expert. It is therefore advisory: it ranks labels for expert review and shows which signal flagged each one.

papers.title: BCR Repertoire Analysis and Cloning of Antibody Candidates Targeting Native and Asp7-Isomerized β-Amyloid.
papers.authors: Nikolaev NA, Myshkin MY, Kolobova EA, Shagina IA, Kechko OI, Varshavskaya KB, Barsova EV, Grigoreva TV, Mitkevich VA, Merzlyak EM, Kozin SA, Makarov AA, Chudakov DM, Lukyanov SA, Grigorova IL, Britanova OV.
papers.abstract: Computational approaches are increasingly used to prioritize monoclonal antibody (mAB) candidates from BCR-seq datasets. However, the reliable identification of B cells encoding antibodies against rare antigenic epitopes remains challenging. We employed a repertoire-guided workflow combining antigen-tetramer sorting of B cells from immunized mice, followed by low-input bulk BCR-seq, which yielded informative clonal repertoires. Clustering analysis allowed us to prioritize IGH and IGK clonotypes potentially targeting β-amyloid and the isoAsp7 proteoform (isoD7-Aβ1-16), implicated in Alzheimer's disease. We observed recurrent IGHV8-12 and IGKV1-117 usage, consistent with canonical mouse anti-Aβ responses. Focusing on isoD7-Aβ-associated candidates, we selected 14 candidate IGH-IGK combinations for recombinant expression including variants containing IGKV8-21, IGKV8-19, IGKV2-112 together with IGHV1-75, IGHV10-1 or IGHV8-12. Several recombinant mABs showed detectable binding activity to isoD7-Aβ, including a candidate with preferential recognition of isoD7-Aβ, supporting the feasibility of the approach but underscoring the challenge of accurate chain pairing. These results provide proof of principle that repertoire-guided analysis can prioritize candidate IGH and IGK chains and propose possible heavy-light chain combinations based on their co-representation across samples while experimental testing remains necessary to identify antibodies with preferential recognition of isoD7-Aβ.

papers.title: Deep Learning Model Based on Automated CT Image Segmentation for Predicting Pathological Complete Response in Lung Cancer Patients Receiving Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy and Chemotherapy: A Multicenter Study.
papers.authors: Zhao J, Gai W, Fang M, He X, Yan X, Li Y, Chen J, Han C, Xu Y, Hong N, Lin G, Du Y, Li Y.
papers.abstract: This study aims to establish a deep learning model based on interactive 3D segmentation to predict NICT efficacy. This study collected 517 NSCLC patients who underwent NICT and surgery at three centers. VISTA3D is applied in this study for CT images to achieve automatic tumor identification in NSCLC patients via automated segmentation combined with point prompts. Multiplex immunofluorescence was performed to compare the tumor immune microenvironment between low-risk and high-risk patients stratified by the model. Based on this model, patients likely to benefit from adjuvant immunotherapy are identified. This model attained AUC values of 0.83 and 0.81 for cohort A and C, with a Dice coefficient reaching 0.83 ± 0.14. Patients identified as high-risk by the model showed a potential survival advantage with adjuvant immunotherapy (HR: 0.55 for DFS; HR: 0.51 for OS). Exploratory multiplex immunofluorescence analysis suggested compositional differences in the tumor immune microenvironment between risk groups. The deep learning model developed in this study, based on interactive segmentation, achieves comparable performance to manual segmentation and assists clinicians in effectively predicting pCR in NSCLC patients undergoing NICT prior to surgical treatment. Furthermore, adjuvant immunotherapy was associated with improved survival in high-risk patients, requiring prospective validation.

papers.title: Acute adverse events associated with commercially available chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell infusions.
papers.authors: Wappler-Guzzetta EA, Shafiq A, Workley L, Dvorak CC, Falcinelli SD, Luu MD, McMillan M, Leavitt A, Nedelcu E.
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy is increasingly used to treat a variety of diseases, but limited data exist on acute adverse events (AEs) associated with these infusions. We aimed to evaluate AEs associated with Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved CAR-T cell infusions in adult and pediatric patients. This was a 5-year retrospective study carried out at a multi-hospital center. Demographic information, disease state, infusion data, medical history, and pre-infusion vitals were extracted from the electronic health record system. Acute AEs were graded per Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) criteria. Associations between AEs and collected variables were analyzed using binary logistic regression and machine learning (random forest classifier) methods. Among 339 adult infusions, 37 AEs were identified (11%): idecabtagene vicleucel 7/40 infusions, lisocabtagene maraleucel 1/39, ciltacabtagene autoleucel 12/104, tisagenlecleucel 5/24, brexucabtagene autoleucel 3/26, and axicabtagene ciloleucel 9/106. Most AEs were grade 1 (54%). Eleven reactions were grade 2, four reactions were grade 3, and two reactions (hypotension, bronchospasm/shortness of breath) were grade 4. No grade 5 AEs occurred. In adults, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) exposure normalized to body weight was associated with a higher acute AE risk (p = 0.007 [binary logistic regression]), supported by machine learning analysis. Among 30 pediatric infusions, one grade 1 hypotensive reaction occurred (~3%). No further statistical analyses were performed in the pediatric cohort because of the limited number of events. FDA-approved CAR-T cell infusions demonstrated a low rate of acute AEs, supporting the safety of current products. The association between increased DMSO exposure and acute AE risk identifies a potential, actionable target for further risk reduction.

papers.title: From prophylaxis to precision immunotherapy via engineering vaccine platforms.
papers.authors: Cabral-Miranda G, Silva JDQ, Hamaguchi B, Giugni FR, Durães-Carvalho R, Cabral-Marques O, Câmara NOS, Sabino EC, Krieger JE.
papers.abstract: Vaccines are evolving from antigen-delivery products into modular technologies designed to elicit specific immune functions. Although prophylactic vaccination aims to establish protective memory before exposure, therapeutic vaccination must redirect immunity in the presence of persistent antigen, immune suppression or pathological tissue remodeling. In this Review, we examine how antigen architecture, innate sensing, antigen-presenting-cell targeting, platform design and administration route jointly determine vaccine-induced immune programmes. We compare the distinct requirements of prevention and treatment, focusing on cancer, chronic viral infection and fibrosis, and assess the opportunities and limitations of RNA vaccines, viral vectors, virus-like particles, adjuvants and combination strategies. We then consider how systems vaccinology and artificial intelligence can inform immunogen design and response prediction, while distinguishing computational promise from experimentally validated benefit. We argue that clinical progress depends on matching each vaccine formulation to a defined biological barrier and demonstrating tissue-level activity, safety, durability and practical deployability. This framework connects vaccine engineering to measurable protective or therapeutic outcomes without assuming that any single platform is universally optimal. By integrating immunological principles with advances in vaccine engineering, this Review provides a conceptual basis for selecting and combining technologies according to disease-specific requirements. Ultimately, this perspective may help guide the development of more precise, adaptable and clinically relevant vaccination strategies, bridging the gap between platform innovation and improved outcomes in prevention and therapy.

figure.label: Fig. 1
figure.caption: Design space for programmable vaccinology. A central decision hub, the “immune program,” integrates five key design inputs: antigen identity, platform architecture, adjuvant/innate programming, delivery route/tissue targeting, and disease context. These inputs collectively shape distinct immune outputs, including neutralizing antibodies, mucosal IgA, tissue-resident memory (T-RM), CD8 + cytotoxicity, Th1/Th2/Th17/Tfh polarization, and tolerance reduction or immune reprogramming. A lower translational layer applies critical filters to each vaccine design, including safety, manufacturability, durability, access, and public trust. This framework illustrates how vaccine components can be rationally combined to program disease-relevant immune responses while maintaining translational feasibility

papers.title: Mapping the In Vitro Landscape of Immunotoxicology Testing.
papers.authors: Corsini E.
papers.abstract: Immunotoxicity assessment is undergoing a transition from traditional animal testing towards mechanistically informed, human-relevant new approach methodologies (NAMs). This transition is particularly important because xenobiotics may disrupt immune homeostasis through immunosuppression or inappropriate immunostimulation, whereas species-specific differences can limit the prediction of human immune responses from animal models. This mini review examines the current landscape of NAMs for immunotoxicity assessment, from established human cell-based assays to computational and advanced experimental models. Skin sensitisation represents the most mature application, demonstrating how adverse outcome pathways, standardised assays and defined approaches can enable regulatory acceptance of animal-free strategies. For immunosuppression, emerging approaches include computational models, the multi-immunotox assay (MITA) and human peripheral blood mononuclear cell-based assays assessing integrated functional endpoints such as antigen-specific antibody production. More advanced platforms, including stem cell-derived immune models, 3D cultures, organoids, microphysiological systems, offer opportunities to better reproduce immune complexity and investigate developmental and systemic immunotoxicity. Integration with (PBK) modeling and quantitative in vitro-to-in vivo extrapolation can further translate NAM-derived concentrations into human-relevant exposure estimates, supporting next-generation risk assessment. Despite substantial progress, important challenges remain, particularly for immunosuppression, autoimmunity, immunostimulation and developmental immunotoxicity. Standardisation, interlaboratory reproducibility, validation, regulatory qualification and clearly defined contexts of use will be essential. Ultimately, integrating complementary in vitro, in silico, mechanistic and computational approaches offers a path towards predictive, animal-free and human-relevant immunotoxicity assessment.

papers.title: Basophil Activation Testing: From Diagnostic Adjunct to Precision Allergy Management.
papers.authors: Catamerò F, Han J, Karabacak DE, Hoffmann HJ, Gibbs BF, Knol E, Mayorga C, Torres MJ, Nopp A, Giovannini M, Mori F, Santos AF, Durham S, Akdis CA, Layhadi JA, Shamji MH.
papers.abstract: Basophils are rare circulating granulocytes that trigger immediate hypersensitivity reactions through IgE-mediated degranulation and also contribute to innate immunity. The basophil activation test (BAT) is a flow cytometry-based functional assay that quantifies basophil reactivity and sensitivity following allergen stimulation, offering a safe, blood-based alternative to in vivo provocation testing. This review summarizes the immunological basis of the BAT, its technical requirements, and its expanding clinical applications across food, respiratory, drug, and hymenoptera venom allergies, autoimmune chronic spontaneous urticaria, and vaccine hypersensitivity. Beyond diagnosis, the BAT increasingly supports monitoring of allergen immunotherapy and biologic treatments, prediction of reaction severity and treatment response, and personalized management decisions. Its performance varies by allergen and clinical context, and wider adoption is constrained by the absence of standardized protocols, validated cut-offs, and reference materials, as well as by basophil non-releasers and dependence on fresh viable blood. Passive BAT and mast cell activation test formats extend testing to patients in whom the conventional BAT is uninterpretable. Automated, data-driven analysis and machine learning-assisted, label-free platforms offer promising routes toward more objective, scalable interpretation. With continued standardization, harmonization, and prospective validation, the BAT is positioned not only as a diagnostic adjunct but as a platform for precision-based allergy management.

papers.title: PIRPath: A region-guided weakly supervised pathomics framework for neoadjuvant immunotherapy response prediction across multiple cancer types.
papers.authors: Yang W, Liu A, Yue J, Zhu A, Bi Z, Shi S, Liu J, Yang J, Yuan P.
papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy is now standard for multiple solid tumors; however, substantial heterogeneity in treatment response remains. Current biomarkers such as programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) capture only limited molecular dimensions of tumor biology. We aimed to predict pathological response from pretreatment hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) whole-slide images (WSIs), benchmark it against PD-L1, and test cross-cancer transferability. Across 320 patients, 377 pretreatment H&E WSIs were processed, yielding 20,247,535 tissue patches. We developed PIRPath (Pathomics for Immunotherapy Response Prediction), a region-guided weakly supervised framework, internally validated in a breast cancer cohort using five-fold cross-validation and further evaluated in two independent external cohorts. Exploratory cross-cancer transfer was assessed in lung cancer and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma cohorts. In breast cancer, PIRPath-BC achieved an AUC of 0.9318 (95% CI, 0.8836-0.9713) in internal validation and external AUCs of 0.7991 (95% CI, 0.6000-0.9509) and 0.7292 (95% CI, 0.5333-0.8947). High-score patients showed significantly higher pathological complete response (pCR) rates than low-score patients in both cohorts (78.6%vs 31.2%, P = 0.010; 70.6% vs 35.3%, P = 0.039). In cross-cancer transfer, PIRPath reached 0.7107 for major pathological response (MPR) and 0.7037 for pCR, versus 0.6125 and 0.4590 for PD-L1. Incremental analyses demonstrated additional predictive value beyond PD-L1. Exploratory transcriptomic analyses linked predictions to reduced stromal features and immune activation-related states. H&E WSIs contain response-associated histological information not fully captured by conventional biomarkers. PIRPath provides a computational pathology framework for extracting this and complementing existing biomarkers in neoadjuvant immunotherapy stratification, although the modest external cohorts require prospective validation.

papers.title: Distinct Treg-Mediated Cardiac Remodeling in HFpEF Mice Treated With Neonatal Mesenchymal Stem Cells and Their Secretome.
papers.authors: Ge ZD, Han J, Takaesu F, Brazhkina O, Mishra R, Sharma S, Chen L, Fu X, Filipp M, Wai CM, Shao NY, Sinha A, Saha P, Puvvala A, Tulshyan A, Ventura L, Thakkar S, Bilewska A, Stefanowicz A, Guru SA, Gunasekaran M, Yang E, Dawn B, Yang P, Shah SJ, Thorp E, Davis ME, Kaushal S.
papers.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction lacks effective disease-modifying therapies. We show that neonatal mesenchymal stem cells and their secretome improve diastolic function by expanding regulatory T cells, reducing inflammation and fibrosis. Our new causal machine learning framework, variable importance prediction for cellular function, identified causal immune pathways driving cardiac functional improvement and revealed regulatory T cells as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Mode of T-cell priming durably shapes the TCR repertoire, effector function, and α4β1 integrin expression of human virus-specific CD4 + T cells.
papers.authors: Antoun E, Liu G, Jayathilaka D, Yao X, Rostron T, Waugh C, Clark K, Sopp P, Fry JW, Xia T, Mentzer AJ, Knight JC, Peng Y, Dong T.
papers.abstract: The generation of an effective T-cell response against an antigen depends on the recognition of the antigen by the T-cell receptor (TCR), followed by T-cell priming, initiating coordinated biophysical, biochemical and proliferative changes that drive differentiation into effector and memory clones. The immunological environments in which priming occurs, such as natural infection or vaccination, influence the quality and persistence of memory T cells, but the long-term impacts remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigate how the mode of priming shapes durable antigen-specific CD4+ T-cell memory, utilising two cohorts 3-4 years after initial antigen encounter: individuals recovered from SARS-CoV-2 infection and infection-naive individuals who received a SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. Using ex vivo single-cell RNA sequencing, paired TCR sequencing and in vitro functional analyses, we characterise the transcriptional, clonal and functional profile of spike-specific CD4+ T cells. Across both cohorts, CD4+ T-cell responses against spike epitopes S166-180, S751-765 and S866-880 were immunodominant, with shared public TCR clonotypes indicating conserved antigen-recognition regardless of mode of priming. Despite this shared specificity, infection-primed individuals exhibited greater diversity of the TCR repertoire and lower convergence of CDR3αβ sequences. Transcriptionally, infection-primed cells exhibited a more cytotoxic and effector phenotype, while vaccine-primed cells preferentially adopted T follicular helper (Tfh)- and Th1-associated phenotypes. Infection-primed individuals also displayed enrichment of cell adhesion and integrin signalling pathways, with a greater proportion of spike-specific CD4+ T cells expressing α4β1 integrin subunits, consistent with enhanced migratory and effector potential. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that the mode of antigen priming may influence long-term CD4+ T-cell memory states, influencing TCR repertoire diversity, functional differentiation and tissue-homing potential, years after the initial immune response.

papers.title: Replication-Stressed Malignant Epithelial Cells Are Associated with CCL18-Positive Macrophage Enrichment in Non-MPR NSCLC After Neoadjuvant Anlotinib plus PD-1 Blockade.
papers.authors: Zhu L, Bao M, Yang F, Wang F, Gao W, Shen Y, Tao B.
papers.abstract: Pathological nonresponse remains common after neoadjuvant immunotherapy-based treatment for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but the cellular states underlying residual disease remain poorly understood. We analyzed post-treatment single-cell RNA-sequencing profiles from 6 patients with NSCLC treated with neoadjuvant anlotinib plus PD-1 blockade, including 3 patients with major pathological response (MPR) and 3 with non-MPR. After quality control, 28,430 cells were classified into major epithelial, immune, and stromal compartments. Reclustering of 18,014 epithelial cells identified 14 transcriptional states, among which E4 was consistently enriched in non-MPR tumors. Copy-number inference revealed substantial aneuploid populations within E4, supporting its malignant origin. E4 cells exhibited a proliferative replication-stress-associated program involving WEE1, CHEK1, TIMELESS, FANCI, and FANCD2. Although closely coupled to cell-cycle activity, this program remained directionally consistent across alternative scoring thresholds and sensitivity analyses. Patient-level integration further showed that aneuploid replication-stress-high epithelial-cell abundance was positively associated with CCL18-positive macrophages displaying lipid-handling, phagocytic, extracellular-matrix-remodeling, and immunoregulatory features. Collectively, these exploratory findings suggest a candidate post-treatment ecosystem in which epithelial cells exhibiting a replication-stress-associated program coexist with a CCL18-enriched macrophage state in tumors without MPR, generating hypotheses for further investigation of residual disease.

papers.title: Peripheral Blood Transcriptomic Candidates Associated With Pseudoexfoliation Syndrome and Pseudoexfoliation Glaucoma: A Bioinformatics Analysis.
papers.authors: Li F, Wang L, Tang G, Wang T, Ma L, Geng Y, Cao X, Tang W, Liu J, Shang Q.
papers.abstract: The molecular mechanism of pseudoexfoliation glaucoma (PXG) is still unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate biomarkers of PXG, with the goal of providing a theoretical basis. Ten blood samples from patients with pseudoexfoliation syndrome (PEX), 10 blood samples from PXG patients, and 10 control blood samples were collected for transcriptome sequencing. A total of three candidate biomarkers (ACTA2, IL1RN, and MMP9) were identified. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed that the three candidate biomarkers were involved in the regulation of the actin cytoskeleton and the leukocyte transendothelial migration pathway. The results of the peripheral immune cell proportion analysis suggested altered peripheral immune profiles among the three groups, involving memory B-cells, CD8+ T-cells, regulatory T-cells, M0 macrophages, and resting CD4+ memory T-cells. Correlation analysis further revealed associations between the candidate biomarkers and these differential immune cell subsets. Exploratory drug‒gene interaction analysis provided preliminary insights for future therapeutic investigations. In an RT-qPCR validation set consisting of 15 peripheral whole blood samples (5 PEX, 5 PXG, and 5 control samples), the mRNA expression levels of the candidate biomarkers were assessed across the three groups. RT-qPCR validation revealed that ACTA2 and MMP9 were significantly upregulated in PXG patients compared with controls, whereas ACTA2, MMP9, and IL1RN were elevated in PEX patients compared with both controls and PXG patients. Collectively, these findings suggest that the three candidate biomarkers may be associated with PEX/PXG-related molecular alterations.

papers.title: CD44+ Proximal Tubular Epithelial Cells May Be Involved in Renal Fibrosis and Inflammation via TGF-β Signaling in Hyperuricemic Nephropathy.
papers.authors: Liang HQ, Deng SH, Liang YQ, Wei QJ, Yin BT, Wang YY, Nong RJ, Li CB, Wang L, Liang XW, Li YJ, Zhao JW, Wei LW, Yu JY, Yan XY, Qin M, Mo QZ, Cheng JW.
papers.abstract: The prevalence of hyperuricemia (HUA) is continuously increasing and HUA may eventually develop into irreversible hyperuricemic nephropathy (HN). Injured proximal tubule (PT) in the HUA microenvironment plays an important role in the progression of HN. However, the underlying pathological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between HUA kidneys and control groups were screened from bulk RNA sequencing data to identify abnormally activated signaling. Subsequently, PT cell-subtypes related to injury and repair were identified in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. Cellular functions of injured PT cells were identified via pseudotime analysis, cell communication analysis, and in silico perturbation. Additionally, spatial transcriptomics and spatial proteomics analyses were combined to validate the expression correlation of signature genes and the functional changes of PT in HUA kidneys. TGF-β signaling-associated genes were upregulated in HUA kidneys. Injured and repairing PT cell subtypes were identified in HUA kidneys with an increased proportion of the Injured subtype and a decreased proportion of the repairing subtype. Spp1 was identified as a signature gene of PT cells and injured PT cells in HUA kidneys. As the receptor of SPP1, CD44 was specifically upregulated in injured PT. Tgfb1 and Tgfbr1 were more highly expressed in the Injured PT subtypes and exhibited spatial overlap with Spp1 and Cd44. In silico perturbation of Cd44 in the Injured cell-subcluster predicted reduced expression of TGF-β signaling-related genes. Cell communication analysis predicted potential associations between CD44+ PT cells and increased SPP1-CD44 axis signaling via autocrine/paracrine SPP1. These predicted interactions may also be linked to TGF-β-associated signaling and to potential pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic functional programs in fibroblasts, macrophages, and dendritic cells (DCs). Additionally, spatial proteomics supported the high expression of TGF-β signaling-related proteins in PT. Computational analyses suggest that CD44+ PT cells are associated with TGF-β-related signaling and may interact with fibroblasts and immune cells through the SPP1-CD44 axis, representing the candidate cell population in the progression of inflammation and fibrosis in HN.
papers.venue: Journal of cell communication and signaling

papers.title: Sepsis-Associated Immunoparalysis: Dynamics, Biomarkers, and Implications for Precision Immunotherapy.
papers.authors: Chooklin S, Chuklin S.
papers.abstract: Sepsis-associated immunoparalysis is increasingly recognized as a dynamic failure of effective host defense rather than an obligatory late phase of sepsis. This narrative review, without quantitative synthesis or meta-analysis, aimed to reassess its biological basis, temporal behavior, measurement, prognostic significance, and therapeutic relevance, while distinguishing mechanistic, prognostic, predictive, and interventional evidence. Current data show that immune dysfunction may arise early, coexist with hyperinflammation, and persist across multiple compartments through reduced monocyte antigen presentation, impaired myeloid maturation and stimulus-induced cytokine responses, lymphocyte depletion and dysfunction, inhibitory signaling, and metabolic or epigenetic reprogramming. No single assay captures this state completely. Monocyte HLA-DR remains the most clinically mature anchor biomarker, particularly when measured serially, whereas functional assays, lymphocyte phenotyping, transcriptomic classifiers, proteomics, and single-cell approaches provide complementary information at increasing operational complexity. Although IL-7 and GM-CSF can modify immune abnormalities, the clinical effectiveness of immune-restorative therapies remains insufficiently established, and unselected immune stimulation may be ineffective or harmful. ImmunoSep tested a combined phenotype-guided strategy: anakinra for macrophage activation-like syndrome and recombinant IFN-γ for immunoparalysis. A prespecified ≥1.4-point decrease from baseline in mean SOFA score across days 2-9 was attained by 35.1% of treated patients versus 17.9% receiving placebo (difference, 17.2 percentage points; 95% CI, 6.8-27.2; P=0.002), without a significant 28-day mortality difference. This supports the combined strategy but does not establish the efficacy of IFN-γ for immunoparalysis alone. Generalizability and management of unclassified patients remain unresolved. Overall, sepsis-associated immunoparalysis is best viewed as a heterogeneous, time-dependent low-response state in which trajectory is part of the phenotype. Future precision-immunotherapy strategies should combine serial bedside-compatible assessment with selective functional or molecular confirmation and test biomarker-enriched, mechanism-matched interventions in prospective multicenter trials.

papers.title: The Inflammatory Response Differences and Associated Mechanisms Between Pre- and Post-Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
papers.authors: Feng Z, Wang G, Kang S, Li K, Li B, Liu X.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to systematically explore the molecular mechanisms underlying end-of-procedure/post-grafting inflammation in coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and identify robust signature genes with therapeutic potential. In this study, public transcriptomic datasets of CABG were integrated for comprehensive bioinformatic analysis. Multiple computational strategies were adopted to screen and verify core inflammation-related signature genes, and a clinical prediction model was established. Immune infiltration characteristics associated with signature genes were further explored. Additionally, clinical samples and in vitro cell experiments were utilized to validate the expression pattern and biological function of key candidate genes. Three inflammation-related genes (IRGs) including CDKN1A, PLAUR and SELE were identified as core signature genes, significantly up-regulated in end-of-procedure/post-grafting CABG samples in both datasets. The nomogram exhibited good calibration and favorable clinical net benefit. Signature genes positively correlated with inflammatory response scores and specific immune cell infiltration (eg, PLAUR with neutrophils). Clinical validation confirmed elevated PLAUR mRNA and protein levels postoperatively, correlating with CRP, IL-6, and TNF-α. PLAUR knockdown reduced inflammatory factor secretion and proliferation of TNF-α-stimulated HASMCs. CDKN1A, PLAUR and SELE may serve as promising candidate biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets regulating CABG end-of-procedure/post-grafting CABG samples inflammation. These findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms and offer a preliminary framework for personalized clinical management, although further validation in large-scale, multi-center cohorts is warranted.

papers.title: Multi-omics and single-cell profiling characterize the protective effects of indole-3-acetic acid in hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury.
papers.authors: He Y, Guan Z, Jia W, Guo W.
papers.abstract: Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is a major cause of liver dysfunction after hepatic surgery and transplantation. Sterile inflammation, myeloid-cell recruitment, and metabolic disturbance contribute to hepatic IRI, but effective immunometabolic interventions remain limited. Indole-3-acetic acid (3-IAA) is a natural plant auxin found in Arabidopsis thaliana shoot apices and young leaves and is also produced by microorganisms. Whether 3-IAA affects hepatic IRI is unknown. We integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling to identify changes associated with hepatic IRI. We then evaluated 3-IAA pretreatment in a murine hepatic IRI model. Serum transaminases and histopathology were used to assess liver injury. CyTOF and single-cell RNA sequencing characterized immune-cell composition, functional signatures, and inferred intercellular communication. Untargeted metabolomic profiling identified 3-IAA among the metabolites showing lower hepatic abundance after IRI. 3-IAA pretreatment lowered alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase levels and reduced histological injury. CyTOF showed lower relative abundances of macrophages and neutrophils after 3-IAA treatment. Single-cell analysis identified fewer Ero1a+Bnip3+ macrophages and more C1qa+C1qb+ macrophages. These changes were accompanied by differences in maturation- and phagocytosis-related signatures. Neutrophil-associated transcriptional programs and inferred CCL, CXCL, MIF, TNF, complement, and galectin signaling also differed between groups. Untargeted metabolomic profiling identified lower hepatic 3-IAA abundance after IRI, and pretreatment with exogenous 3-IAA attenuated liver injury in mice. Protection was associated with changes in macrophage and neutrophil abundance, cell states, and inferred immune communication.
papers.venue: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology

papers.title: B cell-macrophage interactions in colorectal cancer: state coupling, spatiotemporal remodeling, and therapeutic implications.
papers.authors: Zhang Z, Zhang Y, Lin J, Cheng B.
papers.abstract: The immune microenvironment of colorectal cancer (CRC) is characterized by pronounced cellular-state and spatial heterogeneity. B cells and macrophages bridge adaptive and innate immunity, respectively, and engage in bidirectional regulation through antibodies and immune complexes, BAFF/APRIL signaling, cytokines, chemokines, and metabolic cues. These interactions are further shaped by tumor cells, stromal components, microorganisms, and other immune populations within the tumor microenvironment. From the perspective of B cell-macrophage state coupling, this review systematically summarizes the biological foundations and reciprocal communication mechanisms underlying their interactions, with particular emphasis on their dynamic remodeling across different disease stages, tertiary lymphoid structures, distinct spatial niches within tumors, and metastatic progression. We further evaluate how established therapies and emerging experimental interventions influence this cellular network. Current evidence suggests that specific B-cell and macrophage states may form distinct functional combinations within either immune-supportive or immunosuppressive ecosystems. However, direct causal evidence remains limited, and the reproducibility of these associations across independent patient cohorts has yet to be firmly established. Future studies should integrate single-cell sequencing, B-cell receptor clonotype tracking, spatial multi-omics, and functional perturbation approaches to move beyond cellular co-occurrence and computationally inferred communication toward direct validation of functional dependencies. Such efforts will also be essential for determining whether composite state-spatial signatures can improve patient stratification, therapeutic response prediction, and treatment decision-making.

papers.title: Immune cell mediated fibrosis after kidney transplantation: mechanisms and emerging immunomodulatory therapies.
papers.authors: Chen H, Chen X, Yan Y, Zhang L, Kuang Z, Ma L, Wang G.
papers.abstract: Renal allograft fibrosis is a common histological endpoint after multiple injuries, rather than an independent disease entity. Despite modern immunosuppression, recurrent alloimmune injury, ischemia reperfusion injury, infection, donor and recipient related factors, and drug toxicity can converge on interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy. This review examines how innate and adaptive immune responses contribute to the transition from early graft injury to chronic remodeling, with particular emphasis on cellular plasticity and intercellular communication. Human single cell and spatial studies show that immune, tubular epithelial, endothelial, and stromal cells form heterogeneous, stage dependent networks rather than fixed pathogenic populations. We prioritize evidence from human kidney allografts while clearly identifying mechanisms inferred from experimental models. Established immunosuppression remains essential for preventing immune mediated graft injury, whereas regulatory T cell therapies, macrophage state modulation, cytokine blockade, and CD38 directed therapy remain investigational. None has been proven to reverse established allograft fibrosis. Future diagnosis and treatment should integrate Banff histology, donor specific antibodies, donor derived cell free DNA, urinary chemokines, and biopsy-based transcriptomics. Clinical trials should determine whether targeted immunomodulation can slow the progression of allograft fibrosis and preserve long-term graft function and survival.
papers.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: Mast cells at the crossroads of immune microenvironment remodeling in hypoxic pulmonary hypertension: a double-edged sword from degranulation to lipid mediators.
papers.authors: Zhai T, Ma L.
papers.abstract: Hypoxic pulmonary hypertension (HPH) is characterized by persistent pulmonary vascular remodeling and elevated pressure, with immune microenvironment dysregulation driving its progression. Mast cells (MCs), as key innate immune cells, are activated under hypoxia via multiple pathways including ROS/calcium signaling, PI3K, and HIF-1α. Through degranulation, they release pro-inflammatory mediators such as histamine, IL-6, and TNF-α, while also secreting protective lipid mediators like ω-3 epoxides via non-degranulation pathways, thereby bidirectionally regulating vascular remodeling. Activated MCs interact with fibroblasts, macrophages, T cells, endothelial cells, and smooth muscle cells, exacerbating inflammation, immune imbalance, and extracellular matrix deposition through key signaling axes including IL-6, IL-1R1/MyD88, and RhoA-ROCK, thus promoting disease progression. Experimental strategies targeting MC stabilization, IgE-FcϵRIα signaling blockade, and the PAF-AH2-ω-3 epoxide axis have shown therapeutic efficacy. Future studies should utilize single-cell and spatial omics to dissect the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of cellular crosstalk and establish immune-phenotype-guided precision intervention systems, offering new directions for HPH therapy.

papers.title: High-risk pancreatic cancer pathology reveals a B3GNT3-associated glycosylation program.
papers.authors: Lin J, Chen C, Li J, Pan Y.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic cancer has a poor prognosis and marked heterogeneity, whereas existing pathomics models generally lack biological interpretability. We aimed to construct the pathomics prognostic score GlyPath-Risk and explore the molecular states associated with the high-risk phenotype captured by the score. We integrated H&E whole-slide images from TCGA-PAAD and Fujian Medical University Union Hospital (FMUUH), extracted handcrafted and deep-learning features using CellProfiler and an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50, and constructed GlyPath-Risk using a combined LASSO and random survival forest model. Prognostic performance was evaluated in training, internal validation, and FMUUH cohorts. Correlation analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and xCell immune-infiltration estimation were used to investigate associations among GlyPath-Risk, the glycosylation transcriptional program, and the tumor microenvironment. Single-cell transcriptomics, CellChat cell-cell communication analysis, Geneformer virtual perturbation, and B3GNT3 knockdown experiments were used to generate and evaluate candidate biological hypotheses. GlyPath-Risk comprised six pathological features and showed C-indices of 0.88, 0.68, and 0.83 in the training, internal validation, and FMUUH cohorts, respectively. Its association with overall survival remained after adjustment for age, sex, and clinical stage in the reported Cox model (multivariable HR = 1.230). The glycosylation gene set showed the strongest mean absolute correlation with pathological features among 20 post-translational modification classes. WGCNA identified six co-expression modules significantly associated with GlyPath-Risk (BH-FDR < 0.05), including a blue module containing B3GNT3. Immune-cell score analyses showed nominal associations with selected immune- and vascular-related scores, but none of 51 candidate scores reached BH-FDR < 0.05. Single-cell analysis suggested differences in predicted outgoing communication from B3GNT3-high and B3GNT3-low tumor cells, while virtual perturbation identified transcriptional states associated with perturbation sensitivity. B3GNT3 knockdown was associated with reduced proliferation and altered macrophage-associated markers in conditioned-medium experiments. GlyPath-Risk showed prognostic associations across the evaluated cohorts. The score was associated with a B3GNT3-related glycosylation transcriptional program and may be related to immune- and vascular-related transcriptomic features. These findings provide a testable framework for investigating the biological correlates of pathomics scores and nominate B3GNT3 as a candidate molecular anchor requiring independent validation.

papers.title: A knowledge graph-driven literature-based discovery framework for drug repurposing in aplastic anaemia.
papers.authors: Sankar D, Bhasuran B, Oviya IR, Saranya G.
papers.abstract: Aplastic anaemia is a haematological disorder characterized by immune-mediated destruction of haematopoietic stem cells and bone marrow failure. Although immunosuppressive therapies are currently used, their lack of target specificity underscores the need for systematic approaches to identify precise therapeutic targets and explore drug repurposing opportunities. A hybrid computational framework integrating literature-based discovery and database-driven validation was employed to construct a multi-layered biomedical knowledge graph. Semantic predications were extracted from SemMedDB and filtered using Unified Medical Language System semantic types to identify disease-, gene-, and drug-related entities. A tripartite disease-gene-drug network was constructed and subsequently extended into a heterogeneous knowledge graph by incorporating pathway-level interactions derived from enrichment analysis using clusterProfiler and KEGG. Drug-gene associations were further supported using curated resources such as DrugBank and DGIdb. Validation of gene-disease associations was performed using DisGeNET. The constructed knowledge graph revealed key genes, including CSF2, IL6, EPO, HLA-DRB1, and CD4, which are central to immune dysregulation and haematopoietic impairment. Pathway enrichment analysis identified critical pathways such as haematopoietic cell lineage, JAK-STAT signaling, cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, and MAPK/ERK cascades, highlighting the interplay between immune signaling and bone marrow dysfunction. Integration of drug-related predications enabled the identification of both clinically used immunosuppressants and potential repurposing candidates, including mycophenolate mofetil, mizoribine, everolimus, and camostat mesylate. Mechanistic mapping of these drugs to key pathways suggests their potential to modulate aberrant immune responses and restore haematopoietic balance. This study demonstrates the utility of a knowledge graph-based framework for integrating heterogeneous biomedical data to uncover multi-level interactions in aplastic anaemia. The approach enables systematic identification of biologically relevant genes, pathways, and drug candidates, supporting hypothesis-driven drug repurposing. While the findings are supported by literature and database validation, they remain exploratory and warrant further experimental and clinical investigation.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omic mapping of urinary and intrarenal immune landscapes in lupus nephritis identifies convergent inflammatory and fibrotic programs.
papers.authors: Casillas-Muñoz F, Chavarria-Avila E, Hernández-Flores TJ, Aguilar-Vazquez A, Perez-Vazquez F, Márquez-González RM, Topete-Reyes JF, Diaz-Rizo V, Pizano-Martinez O, Gomez-Rios CA, Juarez-Gomez C, Cabrera-López M, Llamas-García A, Vazquez-Del Mercado M.
papers.abstract: Renal biopsy is the gold standard for classifying lupus nephritis (LN), but due to its invasiveness and difficult longitudinal follow-up, it incompletely captures immune and histopathological dynamics. Urinary single-cell transcriptomic analysis has been proposed as a minimally invasive approach for monitoring LN, while renal single-cell and spatial transcriptomics provide high-resolution reference maps of the intrarenal environment. We performed a systematic scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines to evaluate direct urinary-renal transcriptomic concordance and pathway molecular convergence of single-cell, single-nucleus, spatial transcriptomic studies. PubMed/MEDLINE and GEO Datasets were systematically searched on August 27, 2026, to identify this concordance and convergence in LN. Analysis of 53 studies identified just one direct urinary-renal transcriptomic concordance study but broader pathway-level biological convergence evidence. Transcriptomic concordance (Tier I) identified shared interferon-responsive signatures, particularly IFIT1, IFIT3, IFI44, MX1, and OAS1; but pathway convergence studies (supported by Tier II studies) gave insights into major urinary biomarkers, such as CXCL9/CXCL10, IL-16, sCD163, BAFF, and FABP4, linked to renal transcriptomic or histopathological programs. The strongest urinary-renal convergence involved IFN signaling and chemokine-mediated immune trafficking, followed by macrophage-associated inflammation and fibrotic remodeling. Collectively, these signatures and biomarkers support urinary profiling as a complementary minimally invasive strategy for longitudinal monitoring and precision nephrology.

papers.title: Toll-Like Receptors in Mycoplasma Infections: Immunopathogenesis, Cheminformatics, and Machine Learning-Based Insights into TLR-Targeted Therapeutics.
papers.authors: Ishfaq M, Bhutto JA, He Z.
papers.abstract: Mycoplasma species are the minimal-genome pathogens that elicit complex host immune responses involving both protective and pathogenic inflammation. Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are pivotal components of the immune system, recognizing pathogen-associated molecular patterns and damage-associated molecular patterns to initiate immune responses. TLRs recognize Mycoplasma-derived lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA motifs, initiating NF-κB and MAPK signaling cascades. While these pathways are indispensable for microbial clearance, their dysregulation contributes to chronic inflammation, autoimmunity, and tissue damage. Consequently, selective modulation of TLR signaling has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for restoring immune homeostasis. In this study, we summarized the recent advances in delineating the molecular crosstalk between TLRs and Mycoplasma, emphasizing the distinct roles of TLRs in pathogen recognition and immunopathology. In parallel, it integrates a cheminformatics-based analysis of TLR inhibitory ligands retrieved from the ChEMBL database, encompassing over 230 compounds across TLR1-5. Multivariate visualization techniques such as principal component analysis (PCA), uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP), and t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) were employed to map the chemical space and reveal receptor-specific clustering patterns. The analysis identified TLR2 and TLR4 inhibitors as occupying distinct but overlapping chemical regions, characterized by higher molecular weight, lipophilicity, and structural complexity. Correlation and similarity mapping further highlighted scaffold conservation among active ligands, providing a quantitative foundation for rational drug design and structure-activity modeling. Furthermore, we explore how machine learning (ML) and computational modeling are reshaping TLR-targeted drug discovery. ML-driven frameworks facilitate ligand prediction, virtual screening, and structure-activity optimization through deep docking and transformer-based scoring models. Integrative ML approaches also extend beyond ligand discovery to encompass multiomics data integration, biomarker identification, and predictive modeling of host-pathogen interactions and immune responses. By bridging immunological insight with cheminformatics and ML-based analytics, this article outlines a multidisciplinary roadmap for precision immunomodulation in Mycoplasma-associated diseases. The convergence of experimental pharmacology and computational intelligence holds the potential to accelerate the discovery of next-generation TLR-targeted therapeutics, advancing personalized strategies for immune regulation and infection control.

papers.title: Influenza Antibody Repertoires: Linking Cellular, Plasma, and Protective Immunity.
papers.authors: Ippolito GC, McDaniel JR, Lavinder JJ.
papers.abstract: For more than half a century, influenza antibody immunity has been interpreted through bulk serology, hemagglutinin (HA) titers, and, more recently, cellular B-cell repertoires. This review argues that protective immunity requires a more integrated view of cellular, plasma, functional, and predictive antibody repertoires. Single-cell BCR sequencing, monoclonal antibody cloning, antibody proteomics, and analyses of antibody cooperation now show that memory B cells, plasmablasts, long-lived plasma cells, circulating IgG, and immune complexes are related but non-equivalent compartments. Plasma antibody responses display recurring fiducial features, including abundance hierarchies, lineage persistence, donor-specific dominance, recall-biased remodeling, and incomplete correspondence with cellular repertoires. These principles are illustrated by HA-head and HA-stem antibodies, neuraminidase-directed immunity, public antibody classes, DR-motif NA active-site antibodies, and the concept of public plasma immunity. We emphasize that secreted antibodies are Fc-liberated molecules capable of engaging complement, C1q, Fc receptors, immune-complex pathways, and synergistic interactions within polyclonal antibody pools. The next frontier is to define functional and protective repertoires, and to use AI-guided sequence-to-function models to predict antibody breadth, abundance, persistence, Fc activity, cooperation, and protection. Such integration may help transform universal influenza vaccine design from the discovery of exceptional antibodies toward the rational engineering of durable protective repertoires.

papers.title: Immunoinformatic and Structural Design of an Influenza A DNA Vaccine Based on Conserved Nucleoprotein Epitopes and Heat Shock Protein 70 Adjuvant.
papers.authors: Sadeh S, Ghaemi A, Arbab Soleimani N, Moghbeli M, BahramAli G.
papers.abstract: Influenza A is a health concern, as it constantly mutates and changes antigens. The conventional vaccine is not very effective in providing immunity. We have designed and characterized a DNA multi-epitope vaccine based on conserved regions of the influenza A nucleoprotein (NP) and have assessed the immune response. This is a bioinformatics study carried out in 2025 at the Pasteur Institute of Iran in Tehran. Epitopes were predicted using the immune epitope database and were screened for conservancy, antigenicity, toxicity, and allergenicity using the alignment-independent antigenicity prediction server (VaxiJen), toxicity prediction tool (ToxinPred), and allergenicity prediction tool (AllergenFP).The vaccine contains a cell-penetrating peptide (CPP) derived from the hemagglutinin protein, a vascular endothelial growth factor 183 (VEGF-183) signal peptide, a tetanus toxoid (TT) helper peptide (830-844), NP peptides, and two repeats of heat shock protein 70 (Hsp70)(407-426). The peptides are arranged using flexible and rigid linkers. The structure was predicted using the self-optimized prediction method with alignment (SOPMA) and AlphaFold2. The structure was further analyzed using high-ambiguity-driven protein-protein docking (HADDOCK) with human leukocyte antigen (HLA) class I and II and toll-like receptor (TLR) 2 and 4, followed by a 200-ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. The docking study showed proper interaction of the selected peptides with HLA and murine BALB/c (H-2d) major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I and II and the whole vaccine with innate immune system receptors. In silico immune simulation indicated cytokine release and T cell activation patterns. The constructed multi-epitope DNA construct was predicted to be antigenic and non-toxic, with structural stability and immunogenic potential. These computational results support prioritizing this construct for experimental expression and murine preclinical validation (immunogenicity, safety, and protection).

papers.title: Tumour Microenvironment-Associated Transcriptional Groups and a Continuous Molecular Gradient in Vestibular Schwannoma.
papers.authors: Yan C, Gao Q, Pei Z, Zhou Q, Wu X, Fang C, Yao J, Shan Q, Zhu Z, Jia D, Bi Y, Xu H, Lou M.
papers.abstract: Vestibular schwannoma (VS) shows marked clinical heterogeneity. How tissue-level transcriptional variation relates to the tumour microenvironment, operative phenotypes, and systemic immunity is still unclear. Tumour bulk RNA sequencing and paired preoperative high-dimensional flow-cytometric immunophenotyping were analysed in 38 patients with sporadic VS. Consensus clustering and principal-curve modelling defined transcriptional groups and a Molecular Gradient Score (MGS). Pathway analysis, immune deconvolution and public single-cell data from 15 VS characterised these programmes. Signatures were evaluated in two independent cohorts. Associations of transcriptional groups and circulating immune-cell percentages with intraoperative tumour texture and brainstem adhesion were explored using univariable and adjusted analyses. Three transcriptional groups formed a continuous molecular gradient: C1, C2 and C3 showed predominantly proliferation, extracellular-matrix and immune-associated programmes, respectively. Stromal and Immune Scores jointly explained 76.7% of within-cohort MGS variance. Related expression programmes were identified in both external cohorts; the MGS contrast was reproduced in GSE141801 but not in GSE39645 (p = 0.19). C2 remained associated with harder tumour texture after adjustment for tumour size and age, whereas the C3-brainstem-adhesion association weakened after age adjustment. Exploratory peripheral-blood analyses identified nominal associations of total T-cell percentages with texture and natural killer (NK)-cell percentages with adhesion. C3 had higher NK-cell percentages than C1 after age adjustment (p = 0.017), but this association weakened after additional tumour-size adjustment (p = 0.053). C1-C3 represent interpretable tissue-level transcriptional groups within the discovery cohort, with a strong contribution from immune and stromal composition. Together with the MGS, they define a descriptive framework for vestibular schwannoma heterogeneity and highlight testable links with operative phenotypes, particularly the ECM-associated C2-hard-texture relationship. The findings support tissue-level transcriptional programmes rather than fixed tumour-cell-intrinsic states.

papers.title: Multi-omics profiling of primary human B cells activated via distinct stimuli.
papers.authors: Aguiar VRC, Franco ME, Abdel Aziz N, Fernandez-Salinas D, Chiñas M, Colantuoni M, Xiao Q, Hackert N, Liao Y, Cervantes-Diaz R, Todd M, Wauford B, Wactor A, Prahalad V, Laza-Briviesca R, Darbousset R, Wang Q, Jenks S, Cashman KS, Zumaquero E, Zhu Z, Case J, Cejas P, Gomez M, Ainsworth H, Marion M, Benamar M, Lee P, Henderson L, Chang MH, Wei K, Long H, Langefeld CD, Sanders AD, Gewurz BE, Sanz I, Sparks JA, Meidan E, Nigrovic PA, Gutierrez-Arcelus M.
papers.abstract: B cells are central for immunity and immune-mediated diseases (IMD), but how distinct signaling pathways drive diverse activation responses over time is not comprehensively understood. Here, we obtain peripheral blood B cells from 27 female healthy donors for in vitro stimulation, profiling the response at multiple time points using RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq with surface protein markers (CITE-seq), and ATAC-seq. Using diverse stimuli including activation of the B cell receptor (BCR), Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7), TLR9, CD40, and differentiation into double negative 2 (DN2) IgD-CD27-CD11c+CD21- B cells, our analyses uncover activation-dependent B cell states, stimulation-specific transcription factors and regulatory regions, the dynamic response of IMD-associated gene expression, and specific open chromatin regions associated with IMD genetic risk. Furthermore, we also identify a lupus risk variant in an enhancer regulating TNFSF4 expression. The analysis data can be accessed via an interactive browser: https://mgalab.shinyapps.io/bcellactivation . Our findings underscore how profiling the full breadth of B cell activation pathways may be important for understanding B cell biology in health and disease.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics and machine learning identify SQLE as a candidate lipid metabolism gene associated with keratinocyte-Th17 cell crosstalk in obesity-exacerbated psoriasis.
papers.authors: Wei W, Xin S, Zhang D, Zhang F.
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is a systemic, immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease strongly associated with metabolic syndrome and obesity. While dysregulation of systemic lipid metabolism is a known exacerbating factor, the localized metabolic reprogramming within the skin microenvironment and its specific role in driving intercellular crosstalk between structural and immune cells remain largely unknown. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of psoriatic and normal skin with bulk transcriptomic data. Lipid metabolic activity at the single-cell level was evaluated using AUCell. To identify diagnostic hub genes, three machine learning algorithms - LASSO regression, Random Forest (RF), and Boruta - were applied to the bulk dataset. T cell subpopulation heterogeneity and intercellular communication were assessed using Seurat and CellChat. To provide preliminary validation of our bioinformatics findings in vivo, we established an obese-psoriasis mouse model using a High-Fat Diet (HFD) combined with topical Imiquimod (IMQ), evaluated via histological staining, immunohistochemistry (IHC), immunofluorescence and ELISA. ScRNA-seq analysis characterized 8 major skin cell types, revealing a significant expansion of T cells and myeloid cells in psoriatic lesions. AUCell scoring demonstrated that psoriatic keratinocytes exhibited the highest lipid metabolic activity among all cell types, with a significant elevation compared to normal controls. Machine learning on bulk transcriptomics identified four core lipid metabolism genes (SQLE, SPTLC2, PLA2G4D, and PLBD1). SQLE was significantly upregulated in psoriatic keratinocytes and demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy. The analysis of the cell communication network suggested potential communication relationships between SQLE+ keratinocytes and Th17 cells, although the identified ligand-receptor pairs were not specific to Th17 cells. In vivo verification demonstrated that diet-induced obesity significantly exacerbated the psoriasis-like lesions induced by IMQ. Immunohistochemical results showed that high expression of SQLE was located in the keratinocytes area, and the infiltration of CD4+IL17A+ Th17 cells in the dermis increased. Additionally, in the obesity-psoriasis model, ELISA test results revealed that the levels of IL-17A and TNF-α were significantly elevated. Our findings identified SQLE as a candidate molecular link between keratinocyte lipid metabolic dysfunction and Th17 cell-mediated cutaneous inflammation in the context of obesity. Our findings suggest that the SQLE-Th17 pathway is potentially hyperactivated under obese conditions, contributing to psoriasis exacerbation. Targeting SQLE and its downstream metabolic-immune communication pathways represents a promising therapeutic frontier for psoriasis patients with comorbid metabolic syndrome, pending validation through functional studies.
